title: Bridge legacy embeddings & rerank semantics to new API: error normalization and cursor behavior
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Summary: Several customers (enterprise search and vector-store teams) rely on legacy /v1/embeddings and /v1/rerank endpoints that return a cursor-style page token and a proprietary set of error codes. The new unified API surface (redwood.ai/embeddings and /ranking) uses RFC-aligned pagination (opaque page_token) and a normalized error schema. We need a compatibility shim in the control plane that preserves existing client semantics while routing to the modern runtime.

Goal: Implement a lightweight compatibility layer that: 1) maps legacy error codes to the new unified error model and HTTP statuses, 2) supports legacy cursor semantics (offset/limit hybrid tokens) and translates them to new page_token usage, and 3) provides clear telemetry and opt-out for clients that choose to migrate. The shim must be transparent to hosted users and configurable for Dedicated/Private deployments.

Non-goals: Changes to model ranking logic or embedding vector format. No changes to streaming / tool-calling flows in this ticket (those are handled separately), except where error mapping intersects streaming errors.

Why this matters: Customers reported integrations failing after we promoted the unified endpoints in a small rollout. Failures fall into three classes: pagination incompatibility, unrecognized error codes (clients treat as fatal), and inconsistent retry semantics. This causes visible user regressions for critical customers and blocks some Dedicated onboarding flows.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Requests to legacy endpoints with legacy cursor tokens return identical page behavior (same items, stable ordering) for >= 95% of requests in integration tests.
2) Legacy numeric/proprietary error codes are translated to normalized error objects with fields: code (string), status (HTTP numeric), message, and retryable (boolean).
3) Transitional telemetry flags (X-Compat-Version) are present on responses and surfaced in the Console per-route breakdown.
4) Config toggle exists per-tenant to enable/disable shim; default = enabled for hosted.
5) Integration test suite added covering cursor translation edge cases and error mapping.
6) Documentation page published: migration guide with examples for token exchange and error mapping.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (canary): route 5% of legacy-hosted traffic through shim, enable verbose mapping logs, hold for 72h. Phase 2 (widen): 25% -> 50% over 2 days if no regressions. Phase 3: default to 100% for hosted and offer upgrade docs. Dedicated customers will be contacted and offered a per-tenant toggle and migration window. For Private/on-prem, ship as opt-in config and provide migration script for token translation.
Fallback: If token decode fails, return legacy 400 with mapped normalized error and a link to migration doc. For mismatched ordering cases, shim returns a stable ordering flag and a small warning header so clients can detect and opt to re-fetch full page.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for token encoder/decoder with 200+ synthetic cursor permutations.
- Integration suite: replay 10k recorded legacy requests from customer logs and compare item sets between legacy stack and shim-enabled route. Threshold: >=95% identical.
- Chaos test: inject transient kernel slowdown to ensure retryable flag leads to correct client retry behavior.
- Manual verification with two pilot customers (Searchly Inc., DocuFlow) using their staging tenants.
- Add end-to-end GitHub Actions workflow that runs the compatibility integration suite on PRs.
comments: 2025-02-12 Aisha Raman: Created ticket after post-rollout incidents from Searchly. Initial scope drafted and risks enumerated.

2025-02-20 Emily Cho (Eng): Spike complete; decoder can recover 98% of tokens but ambiguous anchors require server-side disambiguation. Proposal: 24h TTL for state blobs, store minimal metadata.
2025-02-26 Design review: DES-311 provided feedback on telemetry header UX. Recommended header: X-Compat-Token-Version and a short human-readable warning for mismatch cases. Design approved.

2025-03-03 Marco Delgado: Canary rollout started (5%). Early logs show two integrations treating mapped errors as fatal due to missing retry_after; adding retry_after for rate_limit and backend_busy mappings.

2025-03-06 Aisha Raman: Updated acceptance criteria to require Console visibility and published migration doc draft. Next: schedule partner calls for Dedicated tenants and prepare PR for shim (github.com/redwood-inference/rw-core/pull/4983).
notes_for_support: Support playbook: If a customer reports broken pagination after upgrade, ask for the request id (header RW-Req-Id). If present, check compat-shim logs for token decode errors. Recommended action: toggle per-tenant shim off and capture failing token for analysis, or exchange token using migration endpoint (POST /compat/migrate-token) to generate canonical page_token.
observability_requirements:
- Add per-route counters: compat_token_decoded_success, compat_token_decode_fail, compat_error_mapped_{code}.
- Sampled 1% ruquests to include full legacy token decode trace in tracing system.
- Console: add small card to per-route page showing compat toggle, decode success rate, and top mapped error codes.
communication_plan:
- Notify pilot customers via CSMs and provide migration guide.
- Postmortem-style summary in #prod-core with links to logs and metrics if regressions seen.
- Docs: publish migration guide and an FAQ on error mappings.
- Customer-facing release notes with timeline and opt-out instructions.
implementation_decisions:
1) Use server-side TTL state blobs rather than embedding offsets in tokens to allow future reordering fixes.
2) Keep mapping table centralized in rw-core to ensure parity across Hosted and Dedicated.
3) Expose an opt-out header X-Compat-Bypass for internal testing only.
4) Do not change ranking/embedding payload structure in this ticket.
open_questions:
- How long should migration TTL be beyond 24h for slow Dedicated customers? (ops input required)
- Should we add automatic token upgrade endpoint that consumes a legacy token and returns a fresh page_token (yes/no)?
- Do we want to add SDK helpers for common clients to decode and migrate tokens?
final_notes: This ticket focuses on minimizing customer regressions while we accelerate adoption of the unified API. Parallel work (ENG-2310) will ensure client SDKs surface clearer migration helpers; coordinate release dates to avoid churn.
